questions.explanation: open-ended questions: Questions for which the patient must provide detail to give an answer.
questions.question: Which term is defined as: Questions for which the patient must provide detail to give an answer.

questions.explanation: An open-ended question requires the patient to provide detail to answer, which is why her story filled in gaps you did not know to ask about. A closed-ended question would have gotten a word or two; noise is anything that obscures a message; ethnocentrism is judging another culture by your own values.
questions.question: You sit down with a patient and ask, "Tell me what happened this morning." She answers with a full story, including details you would never have thought to ask about. You got that detail because you used:

questions.explanation: telemetry: A process in which electronic signals are converted into coded, audible signals; these signals can then be transmitted by radio or telephone to a receiver with a decoder at the hospital.
questions.question: Which term is defined as: A process in which electronic signals are converted into coded, audible signals; these signals can then be transmitted by radio or telephone to a receiver with a decoder at the hospital.

questions.explanation: Telemetry is the process of converting electronic signals into coded, audible signals that a receiver with a decoder can turn back into data. A verbal radio report is you speaking the findings yourself; trunking assigns frequencies from a pool; paging sends alerts to receivers.
questions.question: You attach the ECG, and the monitor converts the tracing into coded, audible signals that travel by radio to the hospital, where a decoder turns them back into the tracing for the physician. Sending patient data this way is called:

questions.explanation: dedicated line: A special telephone line that is used for specific point-to-point communications; also known as a hot line.
questions.question: Which term is defined as: A special telephone line that is used for specific point-to-point communications; also known as a hot line.

questions.explanation: A dedicated line is a special telephone line used for specific point-to-point communications - a hot line that connects two points and nothing else. A cellular telephone communicates through cell sites and can reach many numbers; a base station is radio hardware; a trunked channel is assigned from a shared pool of frequencies.
questions.question: From the emergency department's EMS room, you pick up a special telephone that connects you point-to-point, straight to your dispatch center and nowhere else. This telephone line is a:

questions.explanation: chief complaint: The reason a patient called for help; also, the patient’s response to questions such as “What’s wrong?” or “What happened?”
questions.question: Which term is defined as: The reason a patient called for help; also, the patient’s response to questions such as “What’s wrong?” or “What happened?”

questions.explanation: The chief complaint is the reason the patient called for help - her own response to "What's wrong?" or "What happened?" The chief concern is the condition your assessment finds most urgent, which is not always the same as the complaint.
questions.question: You ask a patient, "What's wrong today?" and she answers, "I've had chest pressure since breakfast." For your report, her answer - the reason she called for help, in her own words - is recorded as her:

questions.explanation: ethnocentrism: When a person considers his or her own cultural values as more important when interacting with people from another culture.
questions.question: Which term is defined as: When a person considers his or her own cultural values as more important when interacting with people from another culture.

questions.explanation: Considering your own cultural values more important - judging another culture's ways as simply wrong - is ethnocentrism. Cultural imposition goes a step further: actually forcing your beliefs, values, and practices on the patient.
questions.question: A crew member rolls his eyes at a family's healing customs and tells them, "Your way of doing this is just wrong - ours is the right way." His attitude is an example of:

questions.explanation: communication: The transmission of information to another person—verbally or through body language.
questions.question: Which term is defined as: The transmission of information to another person—verbally or through body language.

questions.explanation: Communication is the transmission of information to another person, verbally or through body language - your posture sent a message without a single word. Telemetry sends coded patient data to a hospital; a handover transfers care to another provider; trunking assigns radio frequencies.
questions.question: Mid-interview, you cross your arms, sigh, and glance at the door. You have not said a word, but the patient stops talking and looks away, clearly reading your body language. What just took place?
